# Page 3^page=3
©Idaho State University, 2020 SCOPE AND CONTENT NOTE The Works Progress Administration Records contain correspondence, folk tales, interviews, inventories and surveys collected by Vardis Fisher and others for the Federal Writers Project, from 1935 through 1942. The majority of the records focus on eastern Idaho, with some focusing on Utah and Oregon. Also included are some materials for the Historical Records Survey. ARRANGEMENT Arrangement of the collection consists of one (1) series divided into two (2) separate subseries. The first subseries contains incoming and outgoing correspondence pertaining to the Federal Writer’s Project, and research materials including biographies of Idaho pioneers. The second subseries consists of Historical Records Surveys of Idaho and Oregon, and Inventories of County Archives of Idaho.

# Page 4^page=4
©Idaho State University, 2020 BIOGRAPHICAL NOTE The Works Progress Administration Federal Writers Project was part of the New Deal programs implemented by President Franklin D. Roosevelt August and September 1935. The program provided jobs for unemployed writers, editors, and research workers during the Great Depression. The Federal Writers Project’s biggest task was the American Guide. The American Guide included travel guides, essays on the geography, architecture, history, and commerce of each state expect Hawaii. Vardis Fisher was the director for the Idaho Federal Writers Project in 1935. The biggest accomplishment for Fisher and his staff was publishing the Idaho Guide in January 1937. The Idaho Guide was one of the first state guides published that the WPA sponsored. Fisher left the Federal Writers Project in 1939. The Federal Writers Project ended in 1943.

Roosevelt implements the Federal Writers Project, August/September 1935 Vardis Fisher becomes Director of the Idaho Writers Project 1937 The Idaho Guide is published, January 1939 Vardis Fisher leaves his position as director of the Idaho Federal Writers Project 1943 The Federal Writers Project is discontinued
